title: Change-record batch receipt
software_contract: seal_batch(request, audit) validates the entire request before the first audit call, without modifying it. Invalid request or non-callable audit raises ValueError; error text is unspecified. Serialize each event independently using JSON keys sorted lexicographically, separators comma and colon without spaces, ensure_ascii=True, then ASCII bytes. Retain event list order. Starting from 32 zero bytes, replace digest with SHA-256(previous digest bytes + event bytes); call audit(zero-based event index, lowercase hexadecimal digest) once after each step. Return batch_id, event_count, components and final_digest. components contains objects with component and event_count, in component first-appearance order. A batch ID is returned as metadata; it is not part of event encoding or the digest. Empty events yield empty components, no audit calls and 64 zero hex characters. If audit raises, propagate the same exception immediately; do not continue, return a receipt, suppress the error, or roll back already performed audit effects. Event/checkpoint order, all intermediate digests and summary fields are observable requirements. The CLI uses an in-memory audit collector and emits an object with receipt and checkpoints (each has index and digest); it does not write an external ledger. Invalid CLI input yields no successful JSON and a nonzero exit.
input_domain: JSON object with exactly batch_id (nonempty string) and events (finite list). Every event has exactly event_id (unique nonempty string), component (nonempty string) and message (string, may be empty). Duplicate event IDs are invalid even if payloads are identical. Unicode and escaped control characters are permitted. audit is a callable accepting (int, str), with potentially observable effects or exceptions. No numerical event-count limit is imposed. Nonmutation excludes changes deliberately performed by the caller's callback itself.
execution_assumptions: The host must issue every required audit call in input order. Caller callback behavior beyond its declared signature is not assumed.
A digest receipt is not a digital signature or proof of an external ledger commit. There is no key management, network access or deployment in this case.
No measured workload distribution, resource cost or hardware benefit is supplied.
